title: Shortest Directed Paths: Scale and Continuum Limits
result_html:
Let \(M\) be the uniform infinite bipolar-oriented triangulation. Let \(\Delta_n\) be the maximum finite vertex-to-vertex shortest directed-path distance in the unconditioned KMSW cell encoded by \(n\) independent increments, each uniform on \(\{(1,-1),(-1,0),(0,1)\}\). The cell contains its \(n+1\) active edges with their endpoint identifications; missing boundary edges are excluded.

The distance scale. There are deterministic constants \(c,C>0\) such that, for every \(n\ge0\) and \(A\ge1\), \[\mathbb P\!\left[\Delta_n>A(n+1)^{3/8}\right]\le C e^{-cA}.\] For every deterministic choice of medians \(m_n\) of \(\Delta_n\), \[c n^{3/8}\le m_n\le C n^{3/8},\qquad n\ge1.\] The constants do not depend on the chosen medians.

Continuous subsequential limits. Write \(p(e)=(i(e),j(e))\) for the north- and west-going primal Peano times of an edge, rooted at the same edge and oriented to increase along directed paths. Let \(d_M^\bullet(e,f)\) count the minimum number of edges in a directed path starting with \(e\) and ending with \(f\), with \(d_M^\bullet(e,e)=1\). Set \[\begin{aligned} U_n&=\{p(e)/n:e\in E(M)\},\\ W_n&=\{(x,y)\in U_n^2:x\le y\},\\ D_n\!\left(\frac{p(e)}n,\frac{p(f)}n\right)&=\frac{d_M^\bullet(e,f)}{m_n}. \end{aligned}\] Here \(x\le y\) is coordinatewise, and \(\Gamma_n=\operatorname{Graph}(W_n,D_n)\).

The laws of \((W_n,\Gamma_n)\) are tight in \(\mathcal F(\mathbb R^4)\times\mathcal F(\mathbb R^5)\), where \(\mathcal F\) denotes closed subsets with the Fell topology. Every subsequential weak limit is almost surely \[(W,\operatorname{Graph}(W,D)),\] where \(D:W\to[0,\infty)\) is locally bounded and continuous. Every point of the limiting domain has exactly one finite limiting height.

Nontriviality. Every such limiting function is almost surely not identically zero: \[\mathbb P\!\left[\exists\,x\ne y:\ (x,y)\in W,\ D(x,y)>0\right]=1.\] Section 8 derives this from the preceding scale, locality, transverse-compactness, and graph-limit results using independent marked cells. No additional joint convergence with quantum-surface data is assumed.

The limiting graph determines a unique function. Uniqueness of the subsequential law and positive distance for every distinct comparable pair are not asserted.

topic: Directed Distances in Random Planar Maps

title: The Small-γ LQG Dimension Expansion
description:
Proposed asymptotic.  Let \(d_\gamma\) denote the almost sure Hausdorff dimension of the planar \(\gamma\)-Liouville quantum gravity metric, with the Gaussian free field normalized to have logarithmic covariance singularity \(\log(1/|z-w|)\). As \(\gamma\downarrow 0\), the proposed expansion is
\[ d_\gamma=2+k\gamma^{4/3}+o(\gamma^{4/3}), \]
where \(k\) is a deterministic, strictly positive, finite constant. 
 The coefficient is characterized by a Gaussian variational problem. Let \(V_n\) consist of continuous functions on \([0,1]\) that vanish at the endpoints and are affine on each interval of the uniform mesh \(16^{-n}\). Let \((Z_f)\) be the centered Gaussian family with covariance
\[ \begin{aligned}\operatorname{Cov}(Z_f,Z_g)\\ &=\pi\int_0^1\bigl(|f|+|g|-|f-g|\bigr)\,dx.\end{aligned} \]
and set
\[ a_n=\mathbb{E}\sup_{f\in V_n}\left\{Z_f-\frac12\int_0^1|f'|^2\,dx\right\}. \]
The stated theorem gives
\[ \begin{aligned}
0<a_*&=\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{a_n}{n}=\inf_{n\geq1}\frac{a_n}{n}<\infty,\\
k&=\frac{2^{-1/3}a_*}{\log16}.
\end{aligned} \] 
 Equivalently, the planar LFPP exponent satisfies
\[ \frac{\lambda(\xi)}{\xi^{4/3}}\longrightarrow\frac{a_*}{\log16}\quad\text{as }\xi\downarrow0, \]
with parameter relation
\[ \begin{aligned}
\xi&=\frac{\gamma}{d_\gamma},\\
\lambda(\gamma/d_\gamma)&=1-\frac{2+\gamma^2/2}{d_\gamma}.
\end{aligned} \]
This specifies a leading coefficient; its numerical value is not evaluated in the note.

title: Gaussian Fluctuations of LQG Distance
description:
Proposed theorem.  Let \(h\) be a whole-plane Gaussian free field with unit-circle average \(h_1(0)=0\). For each \(0<\gamma<2\), let \(D_h^\gamma\) be the \(\gamma\)-LQG metric, using the same field for all \(\gamma\). Fix its deterministic scale by requiring the lower median of
\[ C_\gamma=\inf_{s,t\in[0,1]}D_h^\gamma(is,1+it) \]
to equal one. These are global distances: the connecting paths are not required to stay inside the unit square. 
 Define
\[ H_y=\int_0^1 h(x+iy)\,dx \]
by \(L^2\) limits of smooth mollifications, and let \(q\) be the lower median of \(\min_{y\in[0,1]}H_y\). The proposed result states that \(q<0\) and
\[ \frac{D_h^\gamma(0,1)-1}{\gamma}\xrightarrow{\mathbb{P}}\frac{H_0-q}{2} \]
as \(\gamma\downarrow0\) on the common field probability space. 
 Consequently the limiting distribution is Gaussian with mean \(-q/2\) and variance \(3/8\). The point-distance median \(m_\gamma=\operatorname{med}D_h^\gamma(0,1)\) also satisfies
\[ m_\gamma=1-\frac{q}{2}\gamma+o(\gamma). \]
Thus the first-order normalization correction comes from minimizing horizontal line integrals across the square.

title: Small-Parameter LQG Geodesics
result_html:
Let \(h\) be a whole-plane Gaussian free field with \(h_1(0)=0\), and let \(P_\gamma:[0,1]\to\mathbb C\) be its almost surely unique \(\gamma\)-LQG geodesic from \(0\) to \(1\), parametrized at constant metric speed: \(D_h^\gamma(0,P_\gamma(t))=tD_h^\gamma(0,1)\). Write \(M_\gamma=\max_{z\in P_\gamma}\operatorname{dist}(z,[0,1])\).

For deterministic \(C<\infty\) and \(\gamma_0>0\), \(\mathbb E M_\gamma\le C\gamma^{2/3}\) and \(\mathbb P[M_\gamma\le a\gamma^{2/3}]\le Ca^{3/5}\), uniformly for \(0<\gamma<\gamma_0\) and \(0<a\le1\). For each \(A\ge1\), \[\limsup_{\gamma\downarrow0}\mathbb P[M_\gamma>A\gamma^{2/3}]\le C(A^{-3}+A^{-4}).\] Thus \(M_\gamma/\gamma^{2/3}\) is tight and bounded away from zero in probability; its inverse moments of orders \(0<r<3/5\) are uniformly bounded for small \(\gamma\).

The entire centered path \[X_\gamma(t)=\frac{P_\gamma(t)-t}{\gamma^{2/3}}\] is tight in \(C([0,1],\mathbb R^2)\) with the uniform topology, and its horizontal component converges uniformly to zero in probability. The proof gives a modulus of continuity through the shared frequency-localized probe estimates. It asserts neither tightness of the full path in \(C^{1/8}\) nor a unique limiting scalar or path law.
source_reference: Theorem 1.1 (deviation), pp. 1–2; Theorem 1.2 (functional tightness), p. 2; shared band-event Lemma 5.1, p. 11; functional proof, §6, pp. 12–13; lower-tail Proposition 7.1, pp. 14–15; scalar consequences, §8, p. 15.

title: Conformal Covariance of Supercritical LQG
description:
Fix \(\xi>\xi_{\mathrm{crit}}\) with \(Q=Q(\xi)\in(0,2)\), and use one fixed normalization of the canonical supercritical Liouville quantum gravity metric. Let \(U,V\subset\mathbb{C}\) be domains, let \(\varphi:U\to V\) be a fixed deterministic conformal bijection, and let \(h\) be a Gaussian free field plus a continuous function on \(V\), in the local sense required to define the metric. Here \(D_h(x,y;V)\) is the internal distance, obtained by minimizing metric length over paths contained in \(V\); it may equal \(+\infty\). 
 Almost surely, simultaneously for every \(u,v\in U\),
\[ \begin{aligned}
D_h\bigl(\varphi(u),\varphi(v);V\bigr)\\
&\quad=D_{h\circ\varphi+Q\log|\varphi'|}(u,v;U).
\end{aligned} \]
The multiplicative constant is exactly one, and the equality includes singular endpoints and infinite distances. The probability-one event may depend on \(\varphi\); the statement is for each fixed map.

title: Higher-Dimensional LFPP Exponents
description:
Fix a dimension \(d\geq2\) and normalize the whole-space log-correlated Gaussian field to have covariance singularity \(\log(1/|x-y|)\). Let \(H_N\) be its smooth white-noise cutoff from scales \(2^{-N}\) to \(1\), using a fixed smooth compactly supported radial kernel as specified in the note, so \(\operatorname{Var}H_N(x)=N\log2\). Let \(a_N(\xi)\) be the median of
\[ \inf_{\substack{P:0\to e_1\\P\subset(-2,2)^d}}\int_P e^{\xi H_N(z)}\,|dz|, \]
where \(e_1\) is the first coordinate unit vector and the infimum is over rectifiable paths. Define
\[ \begin{aligned}
\lambda_d(\xi)&=-\lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{\log a_N(\xi)}{N\log2}\\
&=1-\xi Q_d(\xi).
\end{aligned} \] 
 For each fixed \(d\) there are constants \(c_d,C_d>0\) and \(\xi_d>0\) such that
\[ \frac{c_d\xi^{4/3}}{\log(1/\xi)}\leq\lambda_d(\xi)\leq C_d\xi^{4/3} \]
whenever \(0<\xi<\xi_d\). In particular, \(\log\lambda_d(\xi)/\log\xi\to4/3\). The constants and the small-parameter threshold may depend on \(d\). 
 Under the metric-dimension correspondence
\[ Q_d(\xi)=\frac{d}{\gamma}+\frac{\gamma}{2},\qquad \xi=\frac{\gamma}{d_\gamma}, \]
the same type of bounds holds for \(d_\gamma-d\):
\[ \frac{c'_d\gamma^{4/3}}{\log(1/\gamma)}\leq d_\gamma-d\leq C'_d\gamma^{4/3} \]
for sufficiently small \(\gamma\). These are logarithmic-exponent conclusions; the note does not identify a leading coefficient or establish convergence of \(\lambda_d(\xi)/\xi^{4/3}\).

title: An Axiomatic Metric in Higher Dimensions
description:
Proposed theorem.  Fix \(d\geq 3\) and \(\xi>0\) such that the continuum LFPP distance exponent satisfies \(Q=Q(\xi)>\sqrt{2d}\). The underlying field is the whole-space log-correlated Gaussian field on \(\mathbb{R}^d\), with covariance kernel \(\log(1/|x-y|)\) modulo constants. The proposed result constructs a measurable assignment \(h\mapsto D_h\) of finite metrics inducing the Euclidean topology, defined for this field plus continuous functions. 
 The assignment satisfies four strong axioms: \(D_h\) is a length metric; its internal metric in each deterministic open set \(U\) is determined by \(h\) restricted to \(U\); adding a continuous \(f\) reweights path length by \(e^{\xi f}\); and, for each fixed \(r>0\) and \(z\in\mathbb{R}^d\),
\[ \begin{aligned} D_h(ru+z,rv+z)\\ &\quad=D_{h(r\cdot+z)+Q\log r}(u,v). \end{aligned} \]
almost surely for all \(u,v\). 
 Any two assignments satisfying these axioms at the same parameters are proposed to differ by a deterministic positive factor, simultaneously for all endpoint pairs and continuous field perturbations. For the continuum approximation kernels specified in the manuscript, the proposed result also gives convergence in probability of normalized LFPP metrics, locally uniformly, to this assignment. The approximation assertion is restricted to those kernels.

title: Odd-Dimensional Fields and Quantum Cones
result_html:
Let \(h\) be the whole-space log-correlated Gaussian field on \(\mathbb R^d\), with covariance \(-\log|x-y|\) modulo constants, and let \(S_t=h_{e^{-t}}(0)-h_1(0)\). For odd \(d=2m+1\ge3\), its law is the Brownian moving average \(S_t=\int_0^\infty q_d(u)(B_{t-u}-B_{-u})\,du\), where \(B\) is standard two-sided Brownian motion and \(q_d(u)=(d-2)e^{-2u}(1-e^{-2u})^{(d-4)/2}\). The process has a modification in \(C^{m-1,\alpha}_{\mathrm{loc}}\) for every \(0<\alpha<1\); the increment variance of its \((m-1)\)st derivative is comparable to \(r^2\log(1/|r|)\) as \(r\to0\), uniformly in time, and no \(m\)th mean-square derivative exists.

Writing \(K_d(u)=(1-e^{-2u})^{(d-2)/2}\) and \(H_d=1-K_d\), the memory profile \(M_t(r)=-\int_{-\infty}^t H_d(r+t-s)\,dB_s\), \(r\ge0\), is a continuous function-valued, time-homogeneous Markov state. For every integer \(d>2\), the pair \((S_t,M_t)_{t\ge0}\) is a Markov lift in the Brownian-memory coupling, with an explicit evolution formula. In odd dimension the spectrum is non-rational, ruling out a finite-dimensional linear time-invariant Gaussian state-space representation of \(\partial_tS\).

Fix \(\gamma\in(0,\sqrt{2d})\), \(Q=d/\gamma+\gamma/2\), and \(\beta<Q\). For \(\sigma_b=\inf\{t\in\mathbb R:S_t-(Q-\beta)t=-b\}\), the recentered process \((S_{s+\sigma_b}-S_{\sigma_b})_{s\ge T}\) converges in total variation as \(b\to\infty\), for every fixed \(T\in\mathbb R\), to compatible continuous limits \(S_\infty\). These define the \(\beta\)-quantum cone with radial part \(S_{\infty,s}+\beta s\) and an independent spherical projection. At any deterministic center \(z\), with \(\sigma_b\) defined using the spherical averages centered at \(z\), the rescaled field \[\begin{aligned} h^{(b)}(x)&=h(z+e^{-\sigma_b}x)-h_1(z)\\ &\quad-\beta\log|e^{-\sigma_b}x|-Q\sigma_b+b \end{aligned}\] converges in total variation to this cone on every fixed ball \(B(0,R)\), as a random distribution.
source_reference: Consolidated manuscript: Theorems A–C, pp. 4–5; Theorem 7.1 (sharp regularity), pp. 25–26; Proposition 7.2 (finite linear-state obstruction), p. 26; Theorem 7.3 (memory-state Markov lift), pp. 26–27; Corollary 7.4 (long-time variance), pp. 27–28. Theorem A and the memory-state formulas also hold for every integer d > 2; the cone construction is for odd d.

title: Mesh-Only Convergence for Orthogonal Tilings
result_html:
Let \(d\ge2\) and let \(D\subset\mathbb R^d\) be open. Consider locally finite orthogonal tilings of \(D\) by closed convex polytopes \(P_v\), with marked points \(v\) in their interiors. Two cells are joined across a shared facet, and the line between their marked points is perpendicular to that facet. Give each edge the conductance \[a(v,w)=\frac{\operatorname{vol}_{d-1}(P_v\cap P_w)}{|v-w|}.\] Assume that the maximum tile diameter \(\varepsilon_n\) tends to zero, with no additional cell-shape or cell-volume alternative.

Fix bounded open sets \(U\) and \(K\) with \(\overline U\subset K\) and \(\overline K\subset D\). Let \(h\) be harmonic and \(C^2\) on a neighborhood of \(\overline K\). For sufficiently large \(n\), let \(h_n\) be the unique discrete harmonic function on the marked vertices in \(U\), with boundary values \(h\) at adjacent vertices outside \(U\). Then \[\begin{aligned} &\max_{v\in V_n\cap U}|h_n(v)-h(v)|\\ &\qquad\le C_{d,U,K}\,\lVert h\rVert_{C^2(K)}\,\varepsilon_n^{4/(d+4)}. \end{aligned}\] The planar exponent is \(2/3\). The proof bounds expected exit times of small-volume superlevel sets using the retained Nash, heat-kernel, weighted-energy, and local-clock estimates.

Under the remaining domain hypotheses of the cited Bou-Rabee–Gwynne results, the mesh-only approximation also gives uniform convergence of harmonic measures on balls and convergence of the stopped canonical walk to Brownian motion modulo time parametrization. The canonical transition probabilities are proportional to \(a(v,w)\). The exponent \(2/3\) concerns harmonic-extension error; no quantitative rate for a parametrized random walk is asserted.

title: Sphere Packings and Tangency Tilings
result_html:
Let \(d\in\{2,3,4\}\), let \(\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d\) be any nonempty open set, and fix \(\varepsilon>0\). There is a countably infinite family of closed balls \(B(v,r_v)\subset\Omega\) with pairwise disjoint interiors and \(0\lt r_v\le\varepsilon\). For each ball, intersect the halfspaces bounded by its common tangent hyperplanes with all tangent balls, choosing the halfspace containing \(B(v,r_v)\). The resulting tangency polytope \(P_v\) is bounded, and the polytopes form a locally finite, face-to-face tiling of exactly \(\Omega\).

Two balls are tangent if and only if their polytopes share a facet, and that facet lies in their common tangent hyperplane. Consequently, joining the ball centers across shared facets gives an orthogonal tiling graph. In dimensions 2, 3, and 4 respectively, each tile has at most 6, 12, and 24 facets, and \[B(v,r_v)\subset P_v\subset B(v,C_d r_v),\] where \(C_2=2\), \(C_3=\sqrt{10}\), and \(C_4=3\sqrt2+2\).

No boundedness, connectedness, or boundary-regularity assumption on \(\Omega\) is required. Local finiteness is relative to \(\Omega\), so accumulation at its boundary is allowed. Exact coverage is by the tangency polytopes; the balls need not cover \(\Omega\). The paper gives separate constructions in the three dimensions. The four-dimensional construction includes an exact-integer computer-assisted interpolation step and its complete checker.

title: Reflected Random Walks with Spatial Singularities
description:
Consider a random countable collection of compact connected planar cells with nonempty interiors and pairwise intersections of zero area. Adjacent cells are distinct and intersect, and carry symmetric positive conductances \(c(H,K)\). There is a closed witness \(S\) with \(\mathcal H^1(S)=0\), coverage of \(\mathbb C\setminus S\), spatial local finiteness off \(S\), and connectedness of the induced cell graph along every horizontal or vertical segment avoiding \(S\). The law uses the paper’s geometric environment topology and is carried by a similarity-invariant Borel class admitting these witnesses; no measurable selection of a witness is required. 
 Assume mass transport modulo translations and positive dilations. Write \(a_H=\operatorname{Area}(H)\), \(\pi(H)=\sum_{K\sim H}c(H,K)\), and \(\pi^*(H)=\sum_{K\sim H}c(H,K)^{-1}\). For the cell \(H_0\) containing the origin, the moment assumption is
\[\mathbb E\!\left[\frac{\operatorname{diam}(H_0)^2}{a_{H_0}}\bigl(\pi(H_0)+\pi^*(H_0)\bigr)\right]<\infty.\]
There is a measurable finite-specific-energy harmonic coordinate \(\Phi\) with uniformly sublinear corrector. Graph local finiteness and the null-boundary property follow from the hypotheses. 
 With ergodicity under the same similarities, conditionally on almost every environment, the canonical reflected walk has a conservative recurrent area clock with transition rate \(c(H,K)/a_H\). Every graph end has a unique spatial image in \(S\cup\{\infty\}\), independent of the witness, and the path never reaches an end at spatial infinity. Interpolate ordinary jumps between representatives in the cells and extend through reflection times as in the construction. From every fixed starting cell,
\[(\varepsilon Z_{t/\varepsilon^2})_{t\ge0}\Longrightarrow (B_t)_{t\ge0}\]
locally uniformly in time, where \(B\) has deterministic finite positive-definite covariance \(t\Sigma\). Assigning each visit to \(H\) the exact holding time \(a_H/\pi(H)\) gives the same limit. Uniformity over starting cells depending on \(\varepsilon\) is not asserted.

Consider a random countable collection of compact connected planar cells with nonempty interiors and pairwise intersections of zero area. Adjacent cells are distinct and intersect, and carry symmetric positive conductances \(c(H,K)\). There is a closed witness \(S\) with \(\mathcal H^1(S)=0\), coverage of \(\mathbb C\setminus S\), spatial local finiteness off \(S\), and connectedness of the induced cell graph along every horizontal or vertical segment avoiding \(S\). The law uses the paper’s geometric environment topology and is carried by a similarity-invariant Borel class admitting these witnesses; no measurable selection of a witness is required.

Assume mass transport modulo translations and positive dilations. Write \(a_H=\operatorname{Area}(H)\), \(\pi(H)=\sum_{K\sim H}c(H,K)\), and \(\pi^*(H)=\sum_{K\sim H}c(H,K)^{-1}\). For the cell \(H_0\) containing the origin, the moment assumption is \[\mathbb E\!\left[\frac{\operatorname{diam}(H_0)^2}{a_{H_0}}\bigl(\pi(H_0)+\pi^*(H_0)\bigr)\right]<\infty.\] There is a measurable finite-specific-energy harmonic coordinate \(\Phi\) with uniformly sublinear corrector. Graph local finiteness and the null-boundary property follow from the hypotheses.

With ergodicity under the same similarities, conditionally on almost every environment, the canonical reflected walk has a conservative recurrent area clock with transition rate \(c(H,K)/a_H\). Every graph end has a unique spatial image in \(S\cup\{\infty\}\), independent of the witness, and the path never reaches an end at spatial infinity. Interpolate ordinary jumps between representatives in the cells and extend through reflection times as in the construction. From every fixed starting cell, \[(\varepsilon Z_{t/\varepsilon^2})_{t\ge0}\Longrightarrow (B_t)_{t\ge0}\] locally uniformly in time, where \(B\) has deterministic finite positive-definite covariance \(t\Sigma\). Assigning each visit to \(H\) the exact holding time \(a_H/\pi(H)\) gives the same limit. Uniformity over starting cells depending on \(\varepsilon\) is not asserted.
